bio: If you hear footsteps upstairs when nobody is home, call me first. Archival audio researcher, magnetic tape restorer, and professional skeptic hunter. Don't be boring.

nodes.partnerMessage: Hey {PlayerName}. Random question: do you ever get that weird feeling someone is behind you, even when you know you're alone? Or am I already making this too strange for a dating app?

choices.choiceText: Only when I stay up way too late staring at a screen.
Pretty often, actually. I think my apartment has some weird activity.
You sound like someone who skipped their psychiatric medication today.
Don't look now, but I just checked behind me and there's nothing there.

nodes.partnerMessage: Fair. I'm skeptical too, honestly. Cold air, eye strain, bad lighting... there are usually pretty boring explanations. I just don't like assuming that's the answer before I check.

choices.choiceText: I'm open-minded, just evidence-based. What kind of evidence do you actually collect?
Drafty floorboards and eye strain are empirical physics. Ghost stories are campfire tales.
Is everything a paranormal mystery to you, or do you ever just relax?
What if the chill on the neck is just a micro-spasm in the trapezius muscle?

nodes.partnerMessage: Okay, now I'm curious. What happens there? Things moving, weird sounds, cold spots... or something harder to explain?

choices.choiceText: Things moving when I leave the room. Keys, mugs, notebooks.
Radio static turning into whisper fragments right around 3:00 AM.
Sudden temperature plunges in the hallway, like walking into a meat locker.
I was just playing along. I don't actually believe in fairy tales.

nodes.partnerMessage: Yeah... not exactly the opener I was hoping for. You could've just said you think I'm wrong. I'm actually pretty used to people making jokes about what I do.

choices.choiceText: My bad. Sarcasm is my default reflex when someone catches me off guard.
Enjoy talking to dust motes and microwave hums in your dark room.
I apologize, Evelyn. That was uncalled for. Tell me what you really do.

nodes.partnerMessage: Then we're probably safe for the moment. The creepy part is that sometimes you don't see anything at all. You just notice your body reacting before your brain has figured out why.

choices.choiceText: Wait, the fear frequency? You actually know the acoustic biology behind this.
You are terrifyingly thorough. Remind me never to explore an attic with you.
Does the 18.9 Hz resonance also induce temporal disorientation?

nodes.partnerMessage: Mostly audio recordings, spectrum analysis, thermal readings, old building plans, and whatever else helps rule things out. I'm not interested in convincing myself of a ghost. I'm interested in finding out what actually happened.

choices.choiceText: That's actually fascinating. What's the strangest recording you've ever captured?
Analog tape? Isn't magnetic tape prone to ghost-echo print-through bleed?
County blueprints? You do historical property research too?
How do you filter out environmental 60 Hz electrical mains hum?

nodes.partnerMessage: Honestly, I like skeptics. They keep me from getting sloppy. If something has a normal explanation, I'd rather find it than force a creepy story onto it.

choices.choiceText: Then test me. What's your favorite urban legend you personally debunked?
Sounds like we'd make a balanced team: your obsession and my grounded anchor.
What if you spend your entire youth chasing something that never existed?

nodes.partnerMessage: I do relax. I just don't apparently relax very well. I tell myself I'll stop working after one more recording, then it's suddenly 2 AM.

choices.choiceText: Curiosity is fine, but burnout is real. When was the last time you slept eight hours?
You sound like you live on cold brew and conspiracy forums.
Even radio operators take off their headsets when their shift ends.

nodes.partnerMessage: That could explain one of the sensations. It wouldn't explain every case I've seen, though. That's the part that keeps me interested.

choices.choiceText: Localized air vortexes caused by micro-fissures in masonry?
You've got an answer for everything. I like that.

nodes.partnerMessage: That one gets tricky. Before I blame anything unusual, I'd check sleepwalking, vibrations, shelves that aren't level, even carbon monoxide. The boring explanations come first.

choices.choiceText: Could be carbon monoxide poisoning. Have you checked your ambient detectors?
Maybe my phantom roommate just wants me to do the dishes.
What if it's seismic micro-tremors rattling loose shelving?

nodes.partnerMessage: That one still bothers me. It was just static at first, then there were these little fragments that almost sounded like words. I had to listen to it over and over before I trusted what I was hearing.

choices.choiceText: What did the whisper say when you captured it?
Does spending all your nights in the dark with static ever get lonely?
Isn't that just auditory pareidolia? The brain forcing order onto random chaos?

nodes.partnerMessage: The temperature drop was real enough to show up on the meter. I still don't know what caused it. That's why I keep the raw readings instead of jumping straight to a conclusion.

choices.choiceText: A geometric column? Like a cylinder standing in space?
You describe it with such clinical detachment, it makes it eerie.

nodes.partnerMessage: Oh. Okay. I genuinely thought you were interested for a second there. That's on me. I don't really enjoy being treated like a weird little party trick, though.

choices.choiceText: Wait, Evelyn, I was teasing! Let me hear your actual research.
Have fun chasing spooky wind gusts.

nodes.partnerMessage: Okay. I'll give you another chance. Just talk to me normally and we're good. I actually have some pretty interesting case files open right now.

choices.choiceText: Understood. Tell me about the case file you're working on right now.
I promise to be good. What reel are you currently baking?

nodes.partnerMessage: Thank you. I get defensive because I hear the same jokes all the time. People see 'paranormal researcher' and assume I'm either gullible or trying to scare them for attention. Most of my work is actually pretty quiet.

choices.choiceText: I want the real Evelyn. Tell me how this all started.

nodes.partnerMessage: Yeah, there's some interesting research around infrasound and perception. I'm less interested in saying 'that proves ghosts' and more interested in understanding why people feel something when they can't see anything.

choices.choiceText: Translation dialects... I really like the way your mind works, Evelyn.
So you're more of a scientific detective than a superstitious believer.
Tandy was investigating a medical equipment factory basement, right?

nodes.partnerMessage: Attics are honestly pretty overrated. Most of the time it's insulation, animals, bad wiring, and a lot of dust. The older basements are usually much more interesting.

choices.choiceText: Creepy boiler tunnels? Now you're definitely taking me on our first date.
Tunnels sound like a great place to contract tetanus or get arrested.

nodes.partnerMessage: It can happen, especially when you're tired or somewhere with a lot of low-frequency noise. I've had investigations where I checked the clock thinking I'd been there fifteen minutes, and it had been hours.

choices.choiceText: Ever experienced that time slip yourself during an investigation?

nodes.partnerMessage: Probably the old water station. Around 2:40 in the morning, the recordings picked up a strange harmonic tone across several channels. Then, on playback, there was a breath right beside the microphone. No one was standing near it.

choices.choiceText: Didn't that terrify you?!
Weren't you scared being out there alone in the dark with no backup?
Did you analyze the breath for lung capacity acoustics?

nodes.partnerMessage: Exactly. Print-through can make old recordings sound like the past is bleeding into itself. A lot of people hear a faint voice and immediately call it paranormal. Half the job is making sure it's actually on the tape.

choices.choiceText: Thermal tape baking and signal restoration? Consider the proposal accepted.
Show me the spectral analysis. I want to see the waterfall graph.
Sticky-shed syndrome on Ampex 456 reels is a nightmare to restore.

nodes.partnerMessage: Yeah. Old plans help a lot. Buildings get renovated, sealed off, renamed... sometimes the thing you're looking for is literally behind a newer wall. I like seeing how the place changed over time.

choices.choiceText: What kind of patterns? Secret annexes?
You're a historian wearing a paranormal investigator's coat.

nodes.partnerMessage: Usually notch filters and a lot of cleanup work. Electrical hum can ruin an otherwise useful recording, especially in old buildings with terrible grounding. You learn to recognize it pretty quickly.

choices.choiceText: You are absurdly competent. It's wildly attractive.

nodes.partnerMessage: There was one local legend about a light on a mountain road that people swore belonged to a dead railway worker. Turns out it was headlights bending through a temperature inversion. Five nights of work for one very boring answer.

choices.choiceText: You're like a real-life Scully. Sharp, relentless, and wildly attractive.
Don't the locals get mad when you kill their folklore?

nodes.partnerMessage: That actually sounds useful. You keep me from overthinking everything, and I make sure we don't ignore the weird stuff just because it's inconvenient.

choices.choiceText: Deal. Where do I sign the partner contract?
I'll carry the heavy equipment as long as you promise not to vanish into thin air.

nodes.partnerMessage: I've thought about that more than I'd like to admit. Sometimes I wonder whether I'm actually chasing evidence or just giving myself a reason to keep looking. Then I find something I can't explain, and I'm back at it.

choices.choiceText: Even if the signals are just echoes, you give them meaning by listening.
I want to be there when reality bends for you.

nodes.partnerMessage: Eight hours? I honestly can't remember. I've had a few nights lately where I look up and realize it's morning. Once I get focused on a recording, I stop checking the time.

choices.choiceText: I'm coming over to make you hot chamomile tea and take your headphones off.
You need someone in your life to force you away from the monitor.

nodes.partnerMessage: Cold brew, yes. Conspiracy forums, not really. I prefer old newspapers and actual records. Much less arguing.

choices.choiceText: I make a killer pour-over. You bring the case files, I bring the brew.

nodes.partnerMessage: That's fair. My grandfather used to say you need to know when to take the receiver off the hook. I understand the idea. I'm just not very good at doing it.

choices.choiceText: Let me turn it off for you tonight. Just for an hour.

nodes.partnerMessage: That was one of our first guesses too. We checked for drafts and couldn't find one. I don't know what caused the drop, but that's why I kept the readings instead of writing a conclusion in the report.

choices.choiceText: You test every variable. I have so much respect for your brain.

nodes.partnerMessage: Always. Carbon monoxide is one of the first things I rule out, especially in old buildings. Whatever else is going on, I'm not risking someone getting hurt just because a place has a creepy reputation.

choices.choiceText: I care about your safety above all else, Evelyn.

nodes.partnerMessage: Honestly, I'd settle for a ghost that did dishes. I'd have no complaints. Most of the strange things I've investigated seem completely uninterested in housework.

choices.choiceText: Then let me come over and cook for you while you digitize your reels.

nodes.partnerMessage: We checked the seismic data and there wasn't anything nearby that lined up with the timing. The movement was slow and consistent, which is what made it so hard to dismiss.

choices.choiceText: Okay, that gave me goosebumps.

nodes.partnerMessage: It sounded like 'still waiting.' Very faint, buried under the hum. What got to me wasn't that it sounded scary. It sounded... sad. Like somebody left a sentence behind and never got to finish it.

choices.choiceText: That's hauntingly tragic.
You listen to the forgotten dead because nobody else will.

nodes.partnerMessage: Yeah. More than I usually say. When you spend enough nights alone with headphones on, even your own kitchen feels strangely quiet. People think the work is exciting all the time. A lot of it is just me, a recorder, and no one to talk to.

choices.choiceText: Open it for me, Evelyn. You don't have to listen to the silence alone anymore.
I don't think you're weird at all. I think you're brilliant and brave.

nodes.partnerMessage: That's exactly why I'm careful with EVPs. Our brains are very good at turning noise into familiar patterns. I don't count a recording as interesting just because I can convince myself I heard a word.

choices.choiceText: Rigorous double-blind methodology. You really leave nothing to chance.

nodes.partnerMessage: Pretty much. It was about four feet across from floor to ceiling. You could feel the temperature change the second you stepped into it, and then it was gone a few seconds later.

choices.choiceText: Did you record any ionization readings?

nodes.partnerMessage: If I get scared enough that I stop paying attention, I miss details. So I learned to stay calm even when something feels wrong. It isn't that I'm fearless. I'm just trying not to let the fear make decisions for me.

choices.choiceText: You don't need armor when you're talking to me, Evelyn.

nodes.partnerMessage: Careful. That's how you end up getting invited to some terrible place at 3 AM because I said, 'It'll be interesting.'

choices.choiceText: My boots are laced and my flashlight is packed. Let's go.
Only if we stop for greasy 24-hour diner pancakes on the drive back.

nodes.partnerMessage: Pretty much. I spend most of my time proving people are hearing old pipes, electrical interference, animals, bad acoustics... and then once in a while something doesn't fit. That's the part I care about.

choices.choiceText: Show me your 1% case files. I want to see the real mystery.

nodes.partnerMessage: Yes. That case gets oversimplified online, but the experiment itself is really interesting. You actually know the details? Okay, I'm impressed.

choices.choiceText: A shared nerd frequency. We're on the same wavelength.

nodes.partnerMessage: That is a strangely specific first-date idea. I don't hate it. Coffee afterward is probably non-negotiable, though.

choices.choiceText: I'll hold your hand when the temperature drops. Send me your private link.

nodes.partnerMessage: I get the joke. And yes, I'm annoyingly careful about safety. Permits, boots, masks, all of it. Being curious doesn't mean being reckless.

choices.choiceText: A girl who obeys municipal safety codes. Truly irresistible.

nodes.partnerMessage: Once. I was in an old chapel taking readings and thought maybe fifteen minutes had passed. I got back to the van and it was morning. I still don't know exactly what happened, and honestly, that's one of the few cases that still makes me uneasy.

choices.choiceText: That sounds terrifying and miraculous at the same time.

nodes.partnerMessage: I sat there listening to that recording longer than I probably should have. I didn't feel like I was hearing a monster. I felt like I was hearing somebody who had been forgotten.

choices.choiceText: Do you think we leave a trace behind when we go?
That kind of sensitivity makes you special, Evelyn.

nodes.partnerMessage: Absolutely. I dropped my recorder. My hands were shaking so badly I had to sit down for a minute. I just didn't expect the fear to hit me that hard.

choices.choiceText: Next time, let me hold the recorder so your hands stay warm.
You really chase the unknown like a storm chaser.

nodes.partnerMessage: I was scared. I was sitting there in damp boots, staring at these rusted pipes, wondering why I thought going into an abandoned building alone was a good idea. That's probably when I realized I didn't want to keep doing this completely on my own.

choices.choiceText: You don't have to be alone anymore, Evelyn. I'm right here with you.
What brought you into this field in the first place?

nodes.partnerMessage: I did. The recording had a breath with a pretty distinct wheeze. The old records matched it to one of the workers who died there. I can't prove that's whose voice it was, but the timing was... hard to ignore.

choices.choiceText: You gave that forgotten man his identity back. That's profound.

nodes.partnerMessage: Okay, we're moving extremely fast. 😭 But I'm not exactly complaining. An anechoic chamber is probably the most on-brand wedding venue I could think of.

choices.choiceText: As long as the cake has black velvet frosting, deal. Let's move to OnlyYaps.

nodes.partnerMessage: The waterfall plot is actually the interesting part. There's a repeating pattern in there that shouldn't be where it is. I have the full-resolution version saved in my private files.

choices.choiceText: Send me the vault key. I want to study it with you.

nodes.partnerMessage: Sticky-shed is awful. The binder gets gummy, the tape starts sticking to the heads, and one mistake can damage something you can't replace. Preserving old recordings is half technical work and half trying not to panic.

choices.choiceText: I appreciate the fragile art of preserving lost moments. Just like you do.

nodes.partnerMessage: Mostly sealed-off spaces. Old fever wards, drainage areas, service tunnels... places that were built for a purpose and then covered up when the building changed. I like figuring out what used to be there.

choices.choiceText: You make history feel like an active crime scene. I'm hooked.

nodes.partnerMessage: I'll take sleuth. 'Historian' makes me sound like I spend all day arguing over footnotes. Which... I do, sometimes, but that's not the fun part.

choices.choiceText: The trench coat definitely suits you better.

nodes.partnerMessage: That's new. Usually people just ask why I have six different filters open. 😭 But... thank you. I'll take the compliment.

choices.choiceText: Intelligence is the most attractive frequency there is. Move this to OnlyYaps.

nodes.partnerMessage: Scully was a huge influence. I liked that she kept asking for evidence even when everybody else wanted an easy answer. That part stuck with me.

choices.choiceText: Then let me be your partner in the field. Link me your vault.

nodes.partnerMessage: They were not happy. I get it, though. If you've grown up with a story your whole life, it feels personal when someone comes in and says, 'Actually, it's headlights.'

choices.choiceText: You're a menace to tourist traps and I love it. Move this to OnlyYaps.

nodes.partnerMessage: Fine. Terms are simple: coffee duty rotates, flashlights get backup batteries, and if a room suddenly drops ten degrees, we leave together. No arguments.

choices.choiceText: I will never leave your side, Evelyn. Contract signed.

nodes.partnerMessage: Some of my cases are ridiculously heavy. If you actually carry them without complaining, you can choose the music on the drive back. That's a serious privilege.

choices.choiceText: Heavy lifting is my specialty. Deal.

nodes.partnerMessage: That... actually means a lot. Most people ask me whether I can talk to dead pets. You understood why I care about the work in the first place.

choices.choiceText: Because I see the reverence in you. Take this to your private room.

nodes.partnerMessage: Yeah. I think I'd want someone next to me if something genuinely unexplainable happened. Not because I need rescuing. Just because... it would be nice not to experience it alone.

choices.choiceText: Hold onto it as tight as you need. Link me your vault.

nodes.partnerMessage: You'd really take the headphones away? 😭 Honestly, that sounds nice. I forget what silence feels like when I've been editing all night.

choices.choiceText: Let them drop. You're off-duty with me. Link me your vault.

nodes.partnerMessage: Yeah... I probably do. I tell myself I'm almost done, then suddenly it's sunrise and my eyes feel like sandpaper.

choices.choiceText: I'll be your digital detox partner. Give me your OnlyYaps handle.

nodes.partnerMessage: Okay, that actually sounds like a date I'd say yes to. Coffee, old recordings, and nobody pretending they're interested in ghosts just to impress me.

choices.choiceText: Then let's set it up. Send me your private link.

nodes.partnerMessage: An hour sounds manageable. No headphones, no case files, no checking waveforms. Just sitting somewhere and talking to you sounds... really good right now.

choices.choiceText: Let me give you that paradise. Let's move to OnlyYaps.

nodes.partnerMessage: Thanks. I know I can get a little obsessive, but I really do try to test everything before I make a claim. It's nice when someone notices the work instead of just the creepy stories.

choices.choiceText: Tell me everything in your private channel. Send the link.

nodes.partnerMessage: Thank you. Most people say they want to come on an investigation and then disappear the second they realize it's cold, dark, and there's nowhere to buy coffee.

choices.choiceText: I walk in first. Always. Give me your OnlyYaps link.

nodes.partnerMessage: Fresh garlic and actual food? You might have found the fastest way to get me to stop talking about work for an entire evening.

choices.choiceText: Angel or not, dinner is on me. Send me your private handle.

nodes.partnerMessage: That reaction is pretty normal. Still, standing there at 3 AM with a flashlight while a room does something weird is not exactly relaxing.

choices.choiceText: I don't have to imagine. Let's do it together. Link me.

nodes.partnerMessage: That's how I see it too. Whether the recordings are paranormal or not, they're usually connected to real people and real places. I don't want to turn that into a cheap scare.

choices.choiceText: You have a profound level of empathy, Evelyn. That's what makes you so captivating.

nodes.partnerMessage: I think about that a lot. Sometimes preserving a voice is the closest thing you can do to keeping a person from disappearing completely. And... yeah, being remembered matters to me too.

choices.choiceText: I will never forget you, Evelyn. Let's talk somewhere secure.

nodes.partnerMessage: Exactly. Otherwise you're just hearing what you already wanted to hear. I don't need a creepy recording to be dramatic. I need it to survive someone trying to prove it's wrong.

choices.choiceText: Let me be your double-blind audio reviewer. Send the link.

nodes.partnerMessage: We got a noticeable ion reading right in the middle of the area. I'm still cautious about what it means, but the spike was definitely there.

choices.choiceText: Show me the sensor logs in your vault.

nodes.partnerMessage: That's hard for me. I'm so used to keeping everything controlled that letting someone see me uncertain feels... weird. But with you, it doesn't feel as uncomfortable as I expected.

choices.choiceText: I'll keep you warm, Evelyn. Always. Send me the link.

nodes.partnerMessage: Okay, you might actually survive an investigation. Bring a decent flashlight, spare batteries, and something warm. I refuse to spend four hours hearing you complain about the cold.

choices.choiceText: On it. Lead the way to OnlyYaps.

nodes.partnerMessage: Blueberry pancakes after an overnight investigation? Honestly, that's one of the few traditions I could get behind.

choices.choiceText: Contract locked in. Send me your private vault link.

nodes.partnerMessage: I'll take that. Finding someone who actually gets why I care about this stuff is rarer than it should be.

choices.choiceText: Then let's not fight statistics. Let's make it real on OnlyYaps.

nodes.partnerMessage: It did. I left that building thinking about how little of the world we actually understand. It was exciting... and honestly a little humbling.

choices.choiceText: I want to explore the rest of that reality with you. Link me.

nodes.partnerMessage: Deal. You handle the microphone, I'll handle the readings. That sounds much safer than me trying to do both while pretending I'm not nervous.

choices.choiceText: Unstoppable duo. Link me your private server.

nodes.partnerMessage: My grandfather was a radio operator. When he died, I inherited his old shortwave receiver. I started listening to it late at night and realized how many voices and pieces of history can disappear without anyone noticing. I think that's where this started for me.

choices.choiceText: He would be so proud of the reverence you treat sound with.
You carry his legacy forward every time you press record.
Did he ever tell you stories about ghost ships or anomalous SOS distress calls?

nodes.partnerMessage: That's really what it is for me. People get hung up on the ghost part, but I'm more interested in the person behind the recording and the story that got left behind.

choices.choiceText: You have a noble heart, Evelyn. Let's move this to your vault.

nodes.partnerMessage: Exactly. That's why I love old recordings. They're disappearing while you're listening to them. You only get one chance to preserve what was there.

choices.choiceText: Then let's not waste another second. Send me your private link.

nodes.partnerMessage: That means a lot. He was probably the one person in my family who never thought I was wasting my time. He'd sit there with that receiver and listen to the rain hitting the antenna like it was music.

choices.choiceText: I'll sit on the porch and listen to the antenna wire with you anytime. Send the link.

nodes.partnerMessage: I still keep his old Morse key on my desk. It's next to my audio interface now. Kind of a strange combination, but I like seeing both of them there.

choices.choiceText: Show me on OnlyYaps. I'd love to see your setup.

nodes.partnerMessage: He did. He told me about strange radio loops picked up from ships that had already gone down. Some of the stories were probably weather and signal drift, but the fact that people kept hearing them for years was enough to make me interested.

choices.choiceText: A magnetic ghost in the ionosphere... that's incredible. Show me the file.

nodes.partnerMessage: In a physical sense, sound leaves traces everywhere before it fades. In a human sense... I think so too. Maybe not in some mystical way. More like memories, habits, recordings, the things people leave in other people.

choices.choiceText: Then let's say words that vibrate the plaster with something good.

nodes.partnerMessage: Thanks. I used to think being that sensitive was a weakness. Now I mostly think it just means I notice things other people skip over.

choices.choiceText: Never apologize for who you are to me. Come on, link me your vault.

nodes.partnerMessage: Okay... that was smooth. I'm not even going to pretend it didn't work.

choices.choiceText: Let me hear that heart rate on OnlyYaps. Send the link.

nodes.partnerMessage: Yeah... I think I would like that. It's strange how comfortable this conversation feels considering we matched maybe ten minutes ago. Let's keep talking somewhere a little more private.

choices.choiceText: Then let's take this somewhere quieter. Send me your vault.

nodes.partnerMessage: That's really nice to hear. I'm used to explaining what I do before people decide what they think of me. It's refreshing not having to defend every weird little interest.

choices.choiceText: I want to hear more. Move this to your private channel.

nodes.partnerMessage: Yeah, we're probably not a good match. Take care.
Okay, I'm moving this somewhere a little quieter. My private OnlyYaps vault has the recordings, notes, and case files. Come over there and I'll show you the stuff I don't put on the public profile.
